item.title: Create Models
item.description:
Meshery offers two primary ways to bring models into your system: Create and Import.

  • Import is ideal when you already have a model definition file (e.g., JSON, CSV) and simply want to bring it into Meshery.
  • Create is the recommended approach if you are starting fresh. A wizard in Meshery UI walks you through building a model step by step.

This page walks you through the Create workflow, which gives you full control over naming, styling, and categorizing your model while sourcing its CRDs from GitHub or ArtifactHub.

item.title: Creating a Meshery Design
item.description:
A Meshery Design is the primary unit of configuration management in Meshery. It is a declarative document that describes the desired state of your infrastructure and applications: the components you want, their configuration, and their relationships. You can deploy, share, version, export, and import designs.

See Meshery Designs for a full description of design capabilities.

Ways to Create a Design

Using the Design Configurator in Meshery UI

The Design Configurator is built into Meshery UI. It lists the components of a model, gives each one a form generated from its schema, and shows the resulting design as YAML next to the forms, so you don’t have to write YAML by hand.

item.title: Edge Styles Guide
item.description:
In Meshery, the line that connects components is called an edge. Each edge visually represents a relationship and uses a specific style to communicate its nature.

This guide helps you interpret the most common edge styles you will encounter.

Interpreting Common Edge Styles

Meshery uses a set of default visual styles to provide at-a-glance information about the type of connection an edge represents. While these styles can be customized in the UI, understanding the defaults is key to interpreting component relationships.

item.title: Exporting Models
item.description:

Export a model with Meshery CLI

item.title: Identifying Meshery Components
item.description:
Ever wondered what the different icons and shapes in Meshery represent? Whether you’re looking at a dashboard, a settings page, or a design, you’ll encounter a rich library of visual elements. This guide is here to help you understand what they mean.

The components in Meshery fall into two fundamental categories, distinguished by whether they can be orchestrated (managed) by Meshery during deployment:

  • Semantic Components (Orchestratable): These represent actual infrastructure resources that Meshery can understand and manage during deployment. Examples include Kubernetes resources (like Pods and Services), databases, and other infrastructure components. Meshery will actively manage their lifecycle during deployment.

item.title: Importing and Exporting Designs
item.description:
Importing and Exporting Designs

Import a design to bring infrastructure configuration you already have into Meshery. Export a design to back it up, move it to another Meshery Server, or use it outside Meshery.

A design holds components, such as Deployments and Services, and the relationships between them.

What happens when you import

You can import any of these formats:

  • Meshery Design (YAML, or an OCI image exported from Meshery)
  • Kubernetes manifest (YAML)
  • Helm chart (.tgz archive)
  • Docker Compose file
  • Kustomize package (archive)

Meshery Server identifies the format from the file itself. It converts Helm charts, Docker Compose files, and Kustomize packages to a Kubernetes manifest, matches each resource’s apiVersion and kind to a component in the registry, builds a design from the matched components, and saves the design. Importing does not deploy anything. Deploy the design afterward from Meshery UI or with mesheryctl design deploy.

item.title: Importing Models
item.description:
Import a Model to register its components and relationships with your Meshery Server, for example a model you exported from another server or one you built with mesheryctl model build.

A model imports only if it contains at least one valid Component or Relationship. To create a model from your own CRDs instead, see Creating Models.

Import a model with Meshery CLI

Limitation on importing connections

mesheryctl model import imports Models that contain Components, Relationships, and Policies. It does not import Connection definitions yet.

item.title: Push or Pull a Model Image
item.description:
Use mesheryctl to Push or Pull a Model Image

A Meshery Model can be packaged as an OCI image - a portable, versioned artifact that bundles the model definition together with all of its components and relationships. Because the package is OCI-compliant, it can be moved between Meshery Servers and stored in any OCI-compatible image repository (Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry, AWS ECR, and so on), exactly like a container image.
